<b>Marrowmaws</b> are [[Enemies (Silksong)|enemies]] in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i>. They are giant, bulkier variants of [[Mawling]]s, able to crush smaller creatures with their ridged hide.<ref>Marrowmaw [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"Giant roller of the lowlands. Its ridged hide will crush smaller creatures beneath it."</i></ref>

== Behaviour and Tactics ==
Upon spotting [[Hornet (Silksong)|Hornet]], Marrowmaws cry out before rolling into a ball and charging at her, bouncing off walls and rolling in the other direction, or stopping if they reach an edge. Any other enemies caught in the roll will be killed.

After rolling for long enough, they stop and pant heavily, creating an opening for attack. After a few seconds, they will regain their energy and be able to roll again.

Jumping over their charge and performing a down-slash can be an effective method of defeating them.<br>
Or, if Hornet's [[Needle]] is strong enough, they can be rushed down before they even begin their assault.

Marrowmaws deal {{Damage|2}} on contact.

=== Act 3 ===
[[Black-Threading|Black-threaded]] Marrowmaws have their health doubled. They can gain any of the standard [[Black-Threading#Movesets|void attacks]].

== Location ==
One Marrowmaw can be found in [[Moss Grotto]] behind two hidden entrances directly east of Hornet's starting area, and does not respawn once defeated. In [[Act 3]], it dies, but another Marrowmaw appears near the entrance to [[Weavenest Atla]]. Marrowmaws can more commonly be found in the western section of [[Weavenest Atla]]. Another one appears in the [[Memorium]], east of the area's bench.

== Trivia ==
* If the Marrowmaw in [[Moss Grotto]] has not been killed before [[Act 3]], it will be dead, leaving behind a Void-filled corpse, and preventing its [[Beast Shard]] from being collected.
* In the secret room within the [[Blasted Steps]] full of [[Squirrm]]s, there is a [[Shell Shard]] deposit which loosely resembles a Marrowmaw. It is referred to as a <code>primal_marrowmaw</code> by its file name.
